description:
The CLI dispatch layer in `crates/jit` authors success response shapes that the architecture assigns to `output.rs`, and `CommandExecutor` has grown into a single 163-method surface. This epic restores those boundaries and adds a mechanical guard so the restored shape holds.

## Background

A survey of `crates/jit` at commit 21f9e563 measured about 63,100 production code lines — excluding `#[cfg(test)]` blocks, test-only sibling modules, doc comments, and blank lines — against about 128,000 lines of test. The declared layering holds where it matters: `domain/`, `graph/`, and `query_engine/` contain no filesystem or process access outside test modules, and `declarations/` owns gate and rule semantics for both storage and validation to consume. Four areas depart from it.

`main.rs` is 8,182 lines, of which `run()` is a single 5,981-line match over the command groups. It carries 155 inline presentation branches on the machine-readable output flag and 145 serialization call sites, so success response bodies are authored in dispatch arms rather than in `output.rs`.

`CommandExecutor` carries 161 public and crate-visible methods across 28 `impl` blocks in 25 files. The file-per-command-family split is sound; the single type every consumer must accept is not.

`output.rs` declares 62 public response structs. Among them the per-query family — `ReadyQueryResponse`, `BlockedQueryResponse`, `AssigneeQueryResponse`, `StateQueryResponse`, `PriorityQueryResponse`, `LabelQueryResponse`, `StrategicQueryResponse`, `ClosedQueryResponse` — is one envelope, an optional filter echo beside `issues` and `count`, written out eight times.

Neither workspace crate manifest declares a `[lints]` table and the repository has no `clippy.toml`, so the zero-warning bar exists only inside the gate script and is not reproducible from a bare `cargo clippy`. The integration harness at `tests/common/harness.rs` is pulled into 4 of the 10 suite targets through a `#[path]` include rather than a shared dev-dependency, so it recompiles per including target.

`main.rs` has grown to 9,578 lines since the survey; `run()` now spans lines 2355-8782 and dispatches the 29 `Commands` variants, and the executor surface has grown to 195 methods.

The machine-readable failure path was delegated to a2546471, which is now archived as done. That container delivered a behavioral contract: every arm that accepts the machine-readable flag renders the structured envelope, the exit code equals the envelope code, a definition-derived census guards new arms, and one adopter-facing contract document exists. It left the structure unchanged. `main.rs` still holds at least fifteen parallel JSON-error emitters, among them `command_json_error`, `claim_json_error`, `validate_fix_json_error`, `profile_json_error`, `gate_pass_json_error`, `dep_add_batch_json_error`, the JSON branch of `invalid_argument`, `exit_recovery_failed`, `render_validation_json`, `emit_top_level_json_error`, and the `handle_json_error!` macro (13 uses, `output_macros.rs:70`). It also has 44 inline `std::process::exit(json_error.exit_code().code())` calls among 76 `std::process::exit` calls. The `error_to_error_code` classifier (`main.rs:55-407`, about 353 lines) lives in the binary. Some call sites override it with their own fallback code: gate status labels every failure `GateCheckError` at four sites (`main.rs:4707,4726,4818,4897`), and top-level `jit search` classifies `SearchError` only on the machine-readable path (`main.rs:7210`). The server crate cannot reach the classifier, so it keeps its own `PathReadError`-to-status map (`crates/server/src/routes.rs:348`). `process::exit` also skips `Drop` for the retained mutation session and the linked-checkout annotation guard.

On the argument and output surface, `cli.rs` declares 108 per-command `json: bool` fields. `main.rs` scans raw argv for `--json` at lines 1388 and 2264. Issue filter strings are parsed ad hoc at about 20 sites, with no shared argument group. In the generated schema, 74 of the 120 leaf commands fall back to the generic `CommandResponse`. The other 46 come from a hand-kept match table in `get_output_schema_for_command` (`schema.rs:456`). `output.rs` declares 33 hand-written `count` structs. Some arms print a bare serialized payload outside `JsonOutput::success`: batch-create dry run (`main.rs:3107`), archive candidates (`main.rs:6313`) and serve stop (`main.rs:7919`).

`main.rs` also bypasses `CommandExecutor`. After a mutation it resolves and reloads issues through `storage` (for example `main.rs:3831-3985`), it calls `jit::search` directly (`main.rs:7150`), and it carries its own foreground-serve path (`main.rs:8053-8088`). Fourteen hidden clap stubs (`cli.rs`, `hide = true`) duplicate `COMMAND_HINTS` (`main.rs:1324`). Because the stubs claim those verbs, the parser-level `unknown_subcommand_hint` can never fire for them. Schema extraction ignores `is_hide_set`, so the stubs appear in the schema as ordinary commands. Human rendering is duplicated too: the issue list is rendered in at least five dispatch arms (`main.rs:2048,3221,5653,5676,6473,6606,6651`), the validation report block appears three times, and the archive renderers are identical.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: No success response body is constructed in `crates/jit/src/main.rs`; handlers return typed command or domain results, and rendering and envelope construction belong to the output layer. Commands do not depend on the output layer.
- [hard] REQ-02: `run()` dispatches to per-command-group handlers, and no single function in `main.rs` exceeds 500 lines.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each command family is reachable through a narrow capability type or trait, so invoking one family does not require accepting the whole `CommandExecutor` surface.
- [hard] REQ-04: The per-query response family is expressed as one generic envelope, and each query command still emits the `{"count": N, "<collection>": [...]}` envelope the CLI contract specifies.
- [hard] REQ-05: `CommandSchema::generate()` remains the derivation authority for the command schema after decomposition, and `builtin_global_flags()` and `get_output_schema_for_command` remain reachable from that derivation.
- [hard] REQ-06: Both workspace crate manifests declare a `[lints]` table encoding the zero-warning clippy bar and `unsafe_code = "deny"`, so `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` reproduces the gate's bar without the gate script.
- [hard] REQ-07: The shared integration-test harness compiles once as a shared dev-dependency rather than being `#[path]`-included into each suite target, and the integration-target and executable-byte budgets under `@/invariant/bounded-rust-build-footprint` are re-measured and reported after the change.
- [hard] REQ-08: `scripts/rust-build-budget.sh` fails when `main.rs` exceeds a declared code-line ceiling, reporting through the existing `rust-build-budget:` summary line that `scripts/cargo-ci.sh` consumes.
- [hard] REQ-09: The CLI's human output, machine-readable success output, exit codes, and schema contract carry the same semantics after the refactor as before, except where REQ-11 to REQ-21 change them deliberately. The existing suites pass without assertion rewrites that weaken them, and each deliberate change has a test stating the new contract.
- [hard] REQ-10: The completion report records production code lines for `crates/jit/src` before and after, per module, counted by `scripts/production-lines.py` in its default mode. The epic's whole-crate net production lines, the sum of the first-parent deltas of df129d9e's merges on `main` against baseline dc2ea8706, end at or below +375 (plan D-54). Deletions made by b697a3f7 issues the lead executes count for b697a3f7, not here. The report lists each merge's delta and states the crate total.
- [hard] REQ-11: One library function in `crates/jit` maps an error to its error code, exit code, details and suggestions; `crates/jit/src/main.rs` contains no error classifier and no per-command JSON-error helper or macro.
- [hard] REQ-12: Command handlers return their failures and their non-zero findings outcomes as values; `main` renders the one failure envelope or human diagnostic, and `std::process::exit` is called from a single site.
- [hard] REQ-13: An error's code depends only on its type: no call site substitutes a fallback code, and the human and machine-readable paths exit with the same code for the same error.
- [hard] REQ-14: The server derives each failure's HTTP status from the library classification in REQ-11 and keeps no error-to-status map of its own.
- [hard] REQ-15: `--json` is one global flag: no subcommand declares its own `json` field, and no code scans raw argv for `--json`.
- [hard] REQ-16: Every command that filters issues takes its filters from one shared, flattened argument group that parses them once at the CLI boundary.
- [hard] REQ-17: Every leaf command in the generated schema names a typed success response derived from its handler's response type; no leaf falls back to `CommandResponse`, and no hand-maintained command-path-to-type table remains.
- [hard] REQ-18: Every machine-readable success payload goes through the one success envelope, every list-emitting command uses one generic list envelope type, and no hand-written `count` struct remains.
- [hard] REQ-19: `main.rs` makes no storage call: each mutation returns the updated entity it reports, search runs through `CommandExecutor`, and foreground serve lives in `commands/`.
- [hard] REQ-20: No hidden verb-hint stub remains; a wrong-verb guess gets its hint from the parser-level unknown-subcommand path, and the schema leaves out every command clap marks hidden.
- [hard] REQ-21: Each human rendering shared by several commands (issue list, validation report, gate run status, archive report) has one renderer in `output.rs` that every printing command calls.

## Decisions

- D-05: User-approved reconciliation with plan D-59: result types remain with their command or domain owner; output owns rendering and envelopes, and commands never depend on output. This replaces the conflicting output-owned-type clause of REQ-01.

- D-01: REQ-10 measures the epic's whole-crate net production lines (first-parent merge deltas against dc2ea8706, default mode), which must end at or below zero. This replaces the 8,700 combined-module target of plan D-26. Reductions beyond the plan are commissioned: the 2026-11-04 survey's cuts, the unproduced ErrorCode variants, and a simplification pass over the `command_group!` forms (user decision relayed by just-in-time-6a, 2026-11-04).
- D-02: REQ-10's ceiling is +375 net production lines, the measured projection of the epic's own approved reductions, replacing D-01's at-or-below-zero target. The bulk-update and archive work executed from epic b697a3f7 keeps its own ledger (user decision relayed by just-in-time-6a, 2026-11-04).
- D-03: Uniform findings-stderr rule. In human mode the shared emitter prints every findings outcome's message as a one-line summary on stderr, with the report on stdout; a handler migration that introduces that line does not breach its "human output unchanged" criterion (steward rulings for c9103fcf, 1ac651c7, 06ee9b67 and f87f9b00, consolidated 2026-11-04).
- D-04: Uniform warnings rule. Every success or findings warning goes through `Outcome::with_warnings`: in human mode it prints as a `Warning: ` line on stderr and is suppressed under `-q`; under `--json` it reaches the envelope's shared string `warnings`. No success payload declares its own `warnings`; attributed messages move into the shared field with their subject in the text, while structured findings keep their own named field (for example check-links' `link_warnings`) (steward rulings for 20fc3b92, 1ac651c7, 3f816619 and 9529b9ac, consolidated 2026-11-04).

## Notes

Scope is `crates/` only. The repository's non-Rust mass — `dev/` and `.jit/` — is planning artefact and repository-owned data, not shipped code.

REQ-10's net-line ceiling (user decisions relayed by just-in-time-6a, 2026-11-04; replaces plan D-26's combined-module target) gates completion and is met by removing and simplifying mechanism. Lines moved between modules earn no credit, and a boundary fix is never traded for a smaller count.

`storage/` and `repository_state/` are out of scope. Their size is the transaction kernel that `@/invariant/atomic-writes` and `@/invariant/derived-state-coherence` require, not accidental bulk.

REQ-07's build-footprint budgets and REQ-08's ceiling are calibrated once, after this epic's deletions.

The response-envelope change in REQ-04 alters the generated schema output. The project's greenfield stance accepts breaking changes; no compatibility shim is required.
